text:
Jack St. Ivany needed 2 minutes and 21 seconds to get his first NHL goal, a snap shot from the point that carried about a 1 percent chance of going in by our numbers. The defenseman was a 112th overall pick by the Flyers in 2018 who spent 63 AHL games with Wilkes-Barre/Scranton in 2022-23 scoring no goals, and he opened a night in which WSH beat FLA 4-3 at Capital One Arena.

The score didn't tell the whole story of the night. Brady Tkachuk answered 52 seconds later and then scored on the power play to put FLA up 2-1, and FLA was the better team through the first period by expected goals, which measure the quality of chances. Then the game turned. WSH out-chanced FLA 2.02 to 1.16 in expected goals in the third period, and by our simulations of every shot, WSH deserved to win 55 percent of the time. Pierre-Luc Dubois and Aliaksei Protas each had a goal and an assist, and Dubois's third-period goal made it 4-2. Alex Ovechkin had a 38 percent look late that Akira Schmid stopped.

Sam Bennett's deflection with 47 seconds left made it 4-3, and Matthew Tkachuk finished with three assists, but FLA couldn't find the tying goal. Our facts don't include standings or streaks, so we'll leave the season picture alone. What we can say is that Schmid and Logan Thompson were nearly even against the chances they faced, so this one was decided by the skaters in front of them.
